fieldValues.title: The muSrs restructure sat uncommitted in a worktree for three days
fieldValues.summary: On 2026-10-27, between about 12:00 and 16:00, an agent restructured muSrs into five purpose-shaped areas and recorded the old and new structure, as the owner had asked. Nothing was committed or pushed, so the work stopped at Build: it was invisible to every other session, and main moved 29 commits ahead. It was found on 2026-10-30, committed as found and merged with main (muDemocracy.org#408).
evidence: Worktree ~/dev/.wt/muDemocracy.org/navigation-structure-2026-10-27: 142 uncommitted changes, files dated 2026-10-27 11:59 to 16:00
Recovered: commit 0bf0e03 (as found), merge bcacb57 (one conflict, both sides kept), muDemocracy.org#408
Readability audit: reachability 67% on main, 93% with the restructure
The research thread on human-readable repositories had recorded, wrongly, that no before/after structure record existed: it existed only in the uncommitted worktree
fieldValues.body: An uncommitted worktree is invisible: the desk, the research and other agents all read the default branch, so finished work there looks like work never done. A remedy would be a check that lists worktrees with uncommitted changes older than a day (for example in scripts/wt ls or the desk).
